summary: The highest-performing TJR clips (1M–3.2M views) share one core mechanic: a sharp contrast between 'ordinary path' and 'TJR's path' that lands within the first 2 seconds, either as a visual juxtaposition (graduation vs. Koenigsegg delivery) or a punchy on-screen statement that doubles as the hook ('same age btw.', 'Mindset…'). Luxury lifestyle and aspirational/motivational moments consistently outperform trading-specific content. Very short clips (7–18s) dominate; anything beyond 30s drops off sharply. The caption is almost always minimal — one line or even one word — letting the visual and on-screen text carry the weight. Relatability triggers ('they think success is graduating', 'same age btw') drive massive share/save behaviour because viewers send them to friends.
moments_to_pick: TJR delivering a one-liner mindset or money quote (e.g. a crisp sentence about financial freedom, silence, or not caring what others think)
TJR reacting with genuine emotion — laugh, disbelief, jaw-drop — to a big number, a car, or unexpected news
TJR doing or saying something that implicitly contrasts his lifestyle with a 'normal' 23-year-old's (buying a car, paying cash, skipping college talk)
A memorable stream moment where TJR says something quotable about wealth, work ethic, or his goals in plain language
TJR interacting with a famous car, exotic purchase, or flex moment that has a specific dollar figure attached
Stream reactions to a big P&L swing (win side only per campaign rules) — genuine shock or celebration
hook_examples: Nobody his age thinks like this.
This is what 23 looks like for TJR.
Most people his age are doing what exactly?
title_formula: Lead with a concrete, specific fact or action ('TJR paid $X for…', 'TJR just said the quiet part out loud') + one emotional word or emoji. Keep under 60 characters. Never start with 'When' or 'Watch'. Example: 'TJR paid $3.5M for a car he can't even rev 😭' → write original variation like 'TJR droppe
caption_formula: One punchy sentence max — either the quotable line from the clip itself OR a contrast statement (e.g. 'Their path vs. his path.'). Follow with a line break then hashtags. No emojis in the sentence unless a single one at the end. Do NOT write a paragraph.
avoid: Clips longer than 25 seconds — engagement collapses after that point in this niche
On-screen text in ALL CAPS for subtitles — top clips all use sentence case; it reads cleaner on the face-cam framing
Captions longer than one sentence — the 1M+ posts use one line or even one word
Trading jargon in titles or captions (SPY, NQ, calls, puts) unless the moment is purely a reaction — the viral clips are lifestyle/mindset, not ticker talk
Any clip that could read as mocking TJR, showing a loss angrily, or taking a quote out of context to embarrass him
Gambling or casino references per campaign rules
